library(TraceR)

## Scope of this guide

This is the implementation snapshot reviewed on 2026-11-20, based on TraceR
26.11.1 and the subsequent fixes in this checkout. It describes the current
application, not the historical roadmap. Update it when changing module
interfaces, replacement rules, persistence, or signature formats.

TraceR is an R package containing a Shiny app. The root UI is `inst/app/ui.R`;
the root server is `inst/app/server.R`. Installed packages contain that directory
as `app/`, and `startApplication()` runs it. The source-development entry point
`inst/main.R` calls `devtools::load_all()` before starting the app.

## Ownership and module boundaries

```text
Root server
  current_table --------> Table module (edits current_table)
       |                         |
       +--> Network module       +--> validation feedback
       |    as.graph_tables()
       |    DiagrammeR graph
       +--> Sidebar module (downloads, session data)
  saved_table ----------> unsaved_changes
  pending_replacement --> confirmation --> current_table
  inputs_to_restore ----> updateInput(root input, root session)

Sidebar actions/import requests --> Root server coordination
```

| Owner | Source | Responsibility |
|-------|--------|----------------|
| Root UI/server | `inst/app/ui.R`, `inst/app/server.R` | Module wiring, keys, checkpoints, replacement confirmation, JSON verification, session restore. |
| Shared sidebar | `R/mod_sidebar.R` | Controls, network ZIP handlers, session import/download, action reactives. |
| Table module | `R/mod_table.R` | Editable DT, row operations, optional-column renaming, table feedback, scroll behavior, table JSON download/import. |
| Network module | `R/mod_network.R` | Reactive graph derivation, render availability, click feedback, pan/zoom. |
| Table model | `R/04_tracerTable.R` | Schema constructor, validation, value-based comparison. |
| Conversion | `R/05_graphTables.R` | Mapping TraceR rows into styled DiagrammeR node/edge tables. |
| JSON and signatures | `R/06_tracerTableJson.R` | Pure table serialization, deserialization, signing, verification. |
| Configuration | `R/00_config.R`, `inst/config.yaml` | DataTools import/session configuration. |

The root UI has no module namespace. Each module namespaces its own controls.
The sidebar receives the **root input object** for session downloads; its own
input scope would not include the sibling Table and Network modules.

The Table module receives the mutable `current_table` reactive value. Network
receives the same value but does not mutate it. Its graph is a derived reactive,
not a second authoritative network. The sidebar does not own a checkpoint.

## Working state, checkpoints, and replacements

`current_table` and `saved_table` start as equivalent zero-row tables. Their roles
are deliberately different: editing changes only the working table; Save changes
only the checkpoint. Both are session-local and disappear on session termination.

`unsaved_changes` compares ordered column names and character vectors through
`tracer_table_data_identical()`. Incidental data-frame row names are ignored.
Sorting, filtering, and graph state do not enter this comparison. Reverting an
edit to its checkpoint value clears dirty state without needing another Save.

| Action | Working table | Checkpoint |
|--------|---------------|------------|
| Cell/row/column-name edit | Updated, even if incomplete | Unchanged |
| Save | Unchanged | Updated only if validation has no errors |
| Reset and confirm | Complete checkpoint restored | Unchanged |
| Load Example / Load Empty | Replaced after dirty confirmation when necessary | Unchanged |
| Accepted table JSON import | Verified/validated table replaces work after dirty confirmation | Unchanged |
| Accepted session import | Structurally valid session table replaces work after dirty confirmation | Unchanged |
| Any download | Unchanged | Unchanged |

`request_replacement()` is the root's common gate for loads and imports. It either
applies a replacement immediately when clean or stores it in
`pending_replacement` and opens confirmation. Cancel discards the pending request,
not the current table. `apply_replacement()` installs the table, requests scrolling
to the top, and restores session inputs when supplied. Reset has its own
confirmation handler. Ordinary tab switching is not blocked.

## Table model and validation

A `tracer_table` is `structure(list(data = data), class = "tracer_table")`.
It has one component and exactly eleven character columns. Six required names
are fixed: ID, Label, Type, From, To, Unique identifier. Five optional field names
exist **only** as data-frame column names; do not duplicate them in metadata.
Supplied column order is preserved, and non-character columns are rejected.

`new_tracer_table()` checks structure, not complete content. Content checking is
explicit through `validate_tracer_table()`, which returns `errors` and `warnings`
data frames with `row`, `field`, and `message`. Structural failures skip content
checking. Missing values include NA, empty strings, and whitespace-only strings;
validation does not modify the input.

Completely blank rows are permitted. Populated rows require unique IDs and a
Type of node, capsule, or edge. Edges require endpoints naming nodes/capsules;
edge-to-edge references are errors and unknown endpoints are warnings. References
are resolved only at the current network level.

```{r validation}
table <- createExampleTracerTable()
validate_tracer_table(table)

unresolved <- new_tracer_table(table$data)
unresolved$data$From[unresolved$data$ID == "E1"] <- "missing-node"
validate_tracer_table(unresolved)$warnings
```

Save, table downloads, and table JSON import block **all validation errors** but
allow warnings with visible feedback. Graph conversion blocks both. Session
restore retains the earlier editing-session semantics: structure is checked,
but incomplete content may be restored and reported, without automatically Save.
Pure JSON functions check structure only; Shiny coordinators enforce content
policy. Do not silently make the pure functions stricter than this contract.

## DT updates and import event sequencing

DT uses server-side processing, no pagination, horizontal scrolling, and a
400px scroll viewport. Data cells do not wrap. Ordinary updates use
`DT::replaceData()` without regenerating the widget or resetting view state.
Column-name changes update `column_names`, which triggers a full widget render.
`DT::editData(..., rownames = FALSE)` handles DT's zero-based column coordinates;
do not replace it with one-based manual assignments.

Adding a row clears searches through `DT::clearSearch()` and resets ordering.
A custom client message waits for a DataTables draw with the expected row count
before scrolling to the appended row. This avoids sorting placing a blank row
at the top or a filter hiding it. Whole-table replacements request top scrolling
through the Table module's returned `scroll_to_top()` function.

The table module wraps the DataTools JSON import result as
`list(request_id = counter, data = imported)`. Each nested Accept event registers
a one-time `session$onFlushed()` callback that increments the counter after
DataTools publishes its result. One-time applies to each registration, not the
whole session. The payload read is isolated, so **only the completed counter**
invalidates the import request. This both permits repeated identical files and
prevents a changed payload firing once with the previous ID and again with a
new ID. Preserve these two behaviors when changing the importer.

## Graph derivation

`as.graph_tables()` dispatches to `as.graph_tables.tracer_table()`, returning
`nodes` and `edges` data frames. Blank editing rows are ignored. TraceR IDs map
to sequential numeric DiagrammeR IDs, while `tracer_id`, `tracer_type`, and
`tracer_unique_identifier` retain the original identity fields. Optional metadata
remains in the authoritative table rather than the derived graph.

The conversion owns fixed element styling and labels: ordinary circles, rounded
capsule boxes, and distinct colors. Missing node labels become empty strings;
missing edge labels become a visually blank space to accommodate DiagrammeR's
renderer. Never substitute an ID for a missing label.

The Network module constructs a directed graph using dot and rankdir TB. It
removes the widget for invalid data, reports issues, and renders again when the
table is valid. `renderFlowchart()`, `initialize_graph_zooming()`, and
`displayNodeId()` remain active helpers. The zoom observer handles dynamically
inserted SVGs; click feedback maps numeric graph IDs back to TraceR IDs.

## Table JSON format, version 1

`tracer_table_to_json()` writes an object with exactly `format`, `version`,
`columns`, and `data`. `columns` is an ordered string array; `data` is an ordered
array of row objects with every declared column. Empty data is `[]`. Values are
strings or null, never numeric graph IDs or rendering attributes. NA is JSON
null; empty strings remain empty strings. Column order is taken from `columns`,
not guessed from row objects. JSON version describes the format, not revisions.

```{r empty-json}
cat(tracer_table_to_json(new_tracer_table()))
```

Serialization uses jsonlite with `auto_unbox = TRUE`, null/NA encoded as null,
`pretty = FALSE`, `digits = NA`, and UTF-8 names/values. Deserialization accepts
text, raw bytes, or parsed objects and rejects unsupported versions. DataTools'
list importer uses jsonlite simplification; the adapter also handles data-frame
rows and NA representations of null (including logical NA in all-null columns).

```{r round-trip}
original <- createExampleTracerTable()
original$data$Author[1] <- NA_character_
original$data$Description[2] <- ""
restored <- tracer_table_from_json(tracer_table_to_json(original))
stopifnot(tracer_table_data_identical(original, restored))
stopifnot(is.na(restored$data$Author[1]), restored$data$Description[2] == "")
```

Legacy DiagrammeR graph JSON is not this format. The app rejects it rather than
guessing a migration. Table JSON contains neither saved checkpoints nor root
Shiny inputs.

## Experimental signature contract

Signed downloads are for testing only and may become incompatible with future
versions. Public keys are not yet distributed; private keys will never be shared.
Do not present signatures as user authentication or an audit trail.

The signed version 1 envelope has exactly these fields:

| Field | Value/meaning |
|-------|---------------|
| format | `tracer_table_signed` |
| version | `1` |
| algorithm | `RSA-SHA256` |
| payload | Exact compact unsigned table JSON stored as a JSON string |
| signature | Base64-encoded RSA signature |

The bytes passed to both OpenSSL operations are exactly:

```text
UTF8("TraceR/tracer_table_signed/1\nRSA-SHA256\n" + payload)
```

The prefix has two LF newline bytes; there is no additional trailing newline.
`charToRaw(enc2utf8(...))` produces the byte sequence. Signing and verification
explicitly supply `hash = openssl::sha256`. OpenSSL performs RSA signing; base64
only encodes the signature for JSON transport and does not encrypt the payload.

Verification decodes the signature and uses the envelope's payload string
directly. It never reserializes the parsed table to recreate signed bytes.
Changing payload whitespace, values, row order, or column names/order invalidates
the signature. Changing only outer JSON formatting may not, if the decoded payload
is identical. Metadata must match the supported constants. Verification failures,
missing public keys, and unsupported algorithms are rejected, never downgraded
to unsigned import. SHA-1 remains only in the deprecated graph-signing path.

The signature proves integrity against the configured public key and that the
corresponding private key signed the bytes, assuming proper key custody. It does
not record a user ID, author, timestamp, expiry, or session. Anyone permitted to
use signed download can obtain a new signature for their validated table.
Optional Author values are not trusted identity claims.

## Keys, deployment, and sessions

The root server loads keys independently. When `RUNNING_IN_DOCKER` is set, it
uses `/app/inst/app/private_key.pem` and `/app/inst/app/public_key.pem`; otherwise
it uses package resources `app/private_key.pem` and `app/public_key.pem`.
Missing files produce NULL for that key. Missing or mismatched public keys prevent
signed verification; a missing private key removes the signed download button.
There is currently no USERID/environment authorization condition on signed
downloads. Do not describe local signing as automatically disabled.

Local and server keypairs may differ. Reusing a signed file requires the public
key corresponding to its original signing private key. Independent loading does
not distribute keys or establish new trust automatically. Never publish private
key material in docs, fixtures, logs, or downloads.

Jenkins supplies key files from credentials during its Docker test build. Git
exclusion alone is not proof that a key is absent from built artifacts. Keep
credential handling under deployment ownership; this guide does not prescribe
copying production private keys to local installations.

Session downloads use `DataTools::downloadModelServer()` with
`dat = reactive(list(tracer_table = current_table()))`, root inputs, NULL model,
and `onlySettings = TRUE`. DataTools `.tracer` bundles remain unsigned. The saved
checkpoint is not included. Session import extracts `data$tracer_table`, checks
its class/data-frame structure, requests replacement, then restores matching
inputs through `updateInput()` using the root session. Removed IDs are ignored.
Session serialization captures inputs broadly, including transient widget state;
do not treat it as authenticated persistence or assume temporary upload paths
are portable.

## Tests and documentation workflow

Run from the checkout:

```{r development-commands, eval=FALSE}
devtools::load_all()
devtools::test(filter = "mod-sidebar")
devtools::test(filter = "tracer-table-json")
devtools::test()
devtools::document()
devtools::build()
devtools::check()
pkgdown::build_site()
```

| Test slice | Important contracts |
|------------|---------------------|
| `test-tracer-table.R` | Eleven-column schema, incomplete states, IDs, edge warnings/errors. |
| `test-graph-tables-tracer-table.R` | Identity mapping, fixed appearance, missing labels, strict conversion. |
| `test-mod-table.R` | Shared edits, row operations, optional-column names. |
| `test-mod-sidebar.R` | Controls, Load confirmation, independent key loading. |
| `test-tracer-table-json.R` | JSON/null/order round-trips, RSA-SHA256 verification, tamper detection. |
| `test-mod-network.R` | Derived graph behavior and retained legacy APIs/deprecation signals. |

Use `shiny::testServer()` for reactive behavior and ephemeral RSA keys for
cryptography. Use `lifecycle::expect_deprecated()` for lifecycle assertions;
generic warning assertions can depend on warning verbosity/throttling. Browser
checks are appropriate for DT draw/scroll/edit behavior that headless tests
cannot measure. Never require production keys for new cryptography tests.

The package-check CI tests multiple R/OS combinations. The existing pkgdown
workflow builds the documentation site and publishes it to GitHub Pages. Roxygen
owns the generated NAMESPACE and Rd pages; guide Rmd sources own the articles.
No running Shiny app, production keys, or remote data are needed to build these
guides.

## Legacy APIs and future extensions

Deprecated compatibility entry points include `createExampleGraph()`,
`asGraphList()`, `createGraphFromUpload()` (internal), `updateGraph()`, the old
download/import modules, `check_signature_validity()`, and
`mod_network_sidebar_ui()`. The private/public key parameters on
`mod_network_server()` are also legacy. Their implementations remain available;
new app work should use tracer_table APIs and the shared sidebar instead.

Future features should preserve these rules:

- Keep current_table authoritative; derive graphs instead of synchronizing copies.
- Preserve incomplete editing states and the distinction between errors/warnings.
- Route whole-table replacements through the root confirmation gate.
- Keep Save checkpoints independent from downloads and imports.
- Store optional names only in the data frame.
- Preserve ID mapping and visually blank missing labels.
- Keep completed import counters and isolated payload reads paired.
- Keep signature bytes/versioning explicit; never reinterpret failed signed input.
- Add authenticated identity metadata only through a deliberate new trust/format design.

Nested capsules, hierarchy navigation, permanent storage, templates, multi-network
linking, revision history, configurable appearance, and authenticated authorship
remain future work. The historical `inst/scripts/tasks.md` is a roadmap, not
evidence that those features are implemented. No PEITHO import or AI integration
is part of the current production app.
